title: clustOpt: Quickstart Guide
text: clustOpt uses subject-wise leave-one-cross-validation find clustering resolutions generalize across biological replicates: PC Splitting: Principal components split two independent sets (odd: PC1, PC3, PC5… even: PC2, PC4, PC6…) Training: held-subject, Random Forest trained one PC set predict cluster assignments Evaluation: Clustering quality metrics calculated opposite PC set separation ensures evaluation performed data independent used training, preventing overfitting providing honest assessment clustering reproducibility.

title: clustOpt: Quickstart Guide
text: suggest_resolution() provides two approaches identifying optimal resolutions: "rank" (default): Ranks tested resolutions aggregating median metric values. Works number subjects. "local_optima": Filters resolutions reproducible clustering (low Hellinger distance across subjects), ranks filtered set using rank aggregation curvature-based detection local optima metric curves. Recommended >=10 subjects, Hellinger filter thresholds scale automatically number subjects. plot_rank_metrics() shows per-metric ranks plot_mean_rank() shows aggregate.   tutorial uses default "rank" method. example dataset contains 3 well-separated celltypes, simple rank aggregation sufficient. real-world datasets denser resolution grid ambiguous cluster structure, method = "local_optima" can better identify resolutions sit natural inflection points metric curves. See ?suggest_resolution details.

title: calculate_hellinger_distance — calculate_hellinger_distance
text: Calculate Hellinger distance two probability distributions. Hellinger distance symmetric measure bounded 0 1, 0 indicates identical distributions 1 indicates distributions overlap.

title: calculate_hellinger_distance — calculate_hellinger_distance
code: calculate_hellinger_distance(q, p)

title: calculate_hellinger_distance — calculate_hellinger_distance
text: q Numeric vector representing first probability distribution. Must non-negative sum 1. p Numeric vector representing second probability distribution. Must non-negative, sum 1, length q.

title: calculate_hellinger_distance — calculate_hellinger_distance
text: Numeric value 0 1 representing Hellinger distance.

title: calculate_hellinger_distance — calculate_hellinger_distance
text: Hellinger distance calculated : H(P, Q) = sqrt(0.5 * sum((sqrt(p) - sqrt(q))^2)) Unlike KL divergence, Hellinger distance symmetric: H(P, Q) = H(Q, P).

title: calculate_hellinger_distance — calculate_hellinger_distance
code: # Identical distributions p <- c(0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25) calculate_hellinger_distance(p, p)  # Returns 0 #> [1] 0  # Completely different distributions (no overlap) q <- c(1, 0, 0, 0) p <- c(0, 1, 0, 0) calculate_hellinger_distance(q, p)  # Returns 1 #> [1] 1

title: calculate_kl_divergence — calculate_kl_divergence
text: Calculate Kullback-Leibler divergence two probability distributions. D_KL(Q || P) measures much information lost P used approximate Q. result always non-negative, 0 indicating identical distributions.

title: calculate_kl_divergence — calculate_kl_divergence
code: calculate_kl_divergence(q, p)

title: calculate_kl_divergence — calculate_kl_divergence
text: q Numeric vector representing "true" probability distribution. Must non-negative sum 1. p Numeric vector representing "approximating" probability distribution. Must non-negative, sum 1, length q.

title: calculate_kl_divergence — calculate_kl_divergence
text: Numeric value representing D_KL(Q || P), always >= 0.   Returns 0 distributions identical.

title: calculate_kl_divergence — calculate_kl_divergence
text: KL divergence calculated : D_KL(Q || P) = sum(q * log(q / p)) Note KL divergence asymmetric: D_KL(Q || P) != D_KL(P || Q). q[] > 0 p[] = 0, divergence infinite. implementation requires elements p positive corresponding elements q positive.

title: calculate_kl_divergence — calculate_kl_divergence
code: # Identical distributions p <- c(0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25) calculate_kl_divergence(p, p)  # Returns 0 #> [1] 0  # Different distributions q <- c(0.5, 0.3, 0.1, 0.1) p <- c(0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25) calculate_kl_divergence(q, p)  # Returns positive value #> [1] 0.2180119

Sequential forked (multicore) plans keep single shared precompute, regression default path. per-resolution future_lapply() closure now also captures scalar hold-subject id resolution vector instead full run grid.

title: clustOpt 1.2
text: Added KL divergence (calculate_kl_divergence()) Hellinger distance (calculate_hellinger_distance()) metrics evaluating cluster distribution consistency training held-subjects. Added modularity score (calculate_modularity()) computed precomputed SNN graph. Added MSE MAD scores (calculate_mse_score()) centroid-based cluster quality evaluation. New suggest_resolution() function ranks resolutions using two complementary methods: direct rank aggregation across four metrics, curvature-based local optima detection via second-order finite differences. New summarize_cv_metrics() per-resolution metric summaries. New visualization functions plot_rank_metrics() plot_mean_rank(). Logging improvements make clustOpt messages distinct dependencies.

title: clustOpt 1.2
text: Pre-allocate results list main cross-validation loop instead growing c(), reducing memory allocation overhead many subjects. Use crossprod() instead explicit t() %*% PCA projections, avoiding materialization transposed gene--cell matrices. Use Matrix::crossprod() modularity calculation stay sparse matrix space avoid dense transposition cluster indicator matrix. Replace .call(rbind, lapply(...)) t(vapply(...)) MAD calculation avoid intermediate list allocation. Precompute SNN graph distance matrix per held-subject (shared across resolutions) instead recomputing per resolution. Pre-extract cluster assignments metadata resolution avoid repeated column lookups.

title: clustOpt 1.2
text: verbose parameter now accepts integer levels (0-3) fine-grained control: 0 = silent, 1 = key milestones, 2 = detailed progress, 3 = Seurat output. Backward-compatible: verbose = TRUE maps level 1, FALSE 0. Added per-step timing via [step_name] Xs log messages verbose >= 1.
